findings.issue: SendTrace is a shared first-write-wins cell (Arc<OnceLock>), and JudgeRequest carries it and is cloned. Any clone of a request shares one trace. If a second backend send reuses a cloned request, its record() is silently dropped, and the second row logs the first backend's request_sha256 with no error. r-6 D3 prevents this only by 'the engine creates a fresh SendTrace per send', which is a convention.
findings.recommendation: Make single-use ownership a property of the type, not engine discipline. Options: (a) implement Clone for JudgeRequest by hand so the clone gets a fresh SendTrace; or (b) make the trace belong to one send, with the engine creating it and backends receiving it per judge call rather than on the cloneable request; or (c) have record() return a bool or debug-assert on a second write so reuse is visible. Add a rustdoc comment on the OnceLock saying why shared interior mutation is needed here (RBP-006 justification).
findings.evidence: D8.1/D8.2 (l.590-593) and the sample (l.684-690, 721-725): derive(Clone) on SendTrace, 'later writes ignored', default 'fresh, empty trace' on JudgeRequest. r-6 D3 l.207-213 says 'never shared through a cloned JudgeRequest', which is enforced only by engine code.

findings.issue: The question-kind invariants (choice 2..=255, score 2..=10, noul has no choices or descriptions, descriptions has one entry per choice) are not held by the type. with_kind/with_descriptions are infallible, Deserialize is derived, and the rules run later in a separate 'then the question-kind rules' step. That step is repeated by both sc-jev and sc-jev-backends. Invalid Questions are therefore constructible and the invariant is re-checked per call site.
findings.recommendation: Validate once in sc-decision-schema: a fallible Question or CanonicalJudgePayload constructor, or #[serde(try_from)] on deserialize, or a single CanonicalJudgePayload::validate() that both crates call. Do not keep two copies of the rules. Also model kind as a three-variant QuestionKind { Choice, Score, Noul } with skip_serializing_if = is_choice, so None is not an implicit 'choice' sentinel. This keeps the bytes of existing payloads identical.
findings.evidence: r-5 D1/D2 (l.119-136) and sample l.186-197: Option<QuestionKind> with None meaning choice, builders without validation. The same rules are restated for jev::v1 in comments only (l.208-210).

findings.issue: OrderedMap<K,V>(Vec<(K,V)>) is deserialized 'in document order' with no stated duplicate-key rule, so a body with repeated question or criteria keys is representable and ambiguous. JevQuestion has public variant fields and derived Deserialize, so the '2..=255' and '2..=10' limits in comments are not enforced on that path. CheckRequest derives Deserialize, so to_canonical (used by input_sha256 recovery) can run on an unvalidated body. JevState::Object and the response usage/extra maps are serde_json::Map; the plan says 'no serde_json feature', so these are key-sorted. The 'key order is document order' and 'extra verbatim' claims and the state-object roundtrip are not true for unsorted keys. The key-ordering test uses already-sorted keys (context, inputs, metadata), so it cannot detect this.
findings.recommendation: Have the OrderedMap visitor reject duplicate keys (INPUT_INVALID or RESPONSE_INVALID, with a fix hint). Enforce criteria counts in a validating constructor or try_from used by both from_canonical and Deserialize. Use OrderedMap<String, Value> for JevState::Object. Either state that nested Value objects are key-sorted and the claim is limited accordingly, or drop the 'verbatim' wording. Use an unsorted-key case in test_state_forms_roundtrip and the key-ordering test.
findings.evidence: r-5 sample l.203-223, 231-246; D3 l.139-141 and D5 l.158-164 ('order-preserving maps'); l.170-172 test keys are alphabetical.

findings.issue: RowContext holds SystemTime for session_created_at and ts, but the projection truncates to ms. A row built from a real clock does not equal try_from_fields(to_fields(row)), because SessionLogRow derives PartialEq. The plan's 'test_fields_roundtrip (every fixture line)' passes only because fixtures are ms-aligned. answer_id is a raw String ('r-7 checks non-empty only') beside the typed session_id, and repo is raw String. The ok()/failed() constructors are infallible, so the only check, on answer_id, can run only on the parse path. to_fields can emit an empty answer_id.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a ms-precision timestamp newtype whose constructor truncates, so the type holds what the column stores. Introduce an AnswerId newtype next to SessionId (a validated 26-char Crockford ULID in r-7; r-6 swaps in Ulid). Keep repo text, but document the lossy-path rule on RowContext. Alternatively make ok()/failed() fallible.
findings.evidence: D6.1 and RowContext sample l.762-779: 'answer_id: String // ULID text from r-6; r-7 checks non-empty only'; 'SystemTime ... written RFC 3339 UTC, ms'. r-6 l.368-369 builds answer_id with Ulid::new().to_string().

findings.issue: The variant seam cannot deliver the claim 'a future local model adds a variant, a module and one schema_for arm; no caller signature changes'. schema_for(ModelFamily) returns only a DecisionSchemaId. DecisionSchema has an associated const and associated types and no receiver, so it is not object-safe and has no runtime lookup from DecisionSchemaId or ModelFamily to an implementation. Backends choose at runtime by the model's family. Each new family therefore needs a hand-written match in every consumer (llm::v1::parse_output hard-wires Canonical). The static-vs-dynamic dispatch intent is not stated.
findings.recommendation: State that dispatch is static and keyed by SchemaFamily. Add one object-safe dispatch function in sc-decision-schema, e.g. llm::parse_output(id: DecisionSchemaId, text, payload), that is the only match on SchemaFamily. New families then edit that crate only. Alternatively drop the trait until a second variant exists and keep Canonical as plain functions.
findings.evidence: D5 (l.437-449) and sample l.742-751. D4.2 has parse_output call variants::Canonical::answers directly.

findings.issue: Two binding signatures disagree and one fake failure path loses data. (1) Sha256Digest::of takes &str (r-7 D2.5, r-6 l.318), but MockJudgeBackend::with_sent_body(body: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) is documented as 'records Sha256Digest::of(body)' (l.340-343, 214-216), which does not type-check. (2) send_with_busy_retry hashes only 'if let Ok(text) = from_utf8(request.body())', and the comment calls the Err arm 'unreachable in practice'. A non-UTF-8 body silently leaves request_sha256 null, contradicting 'SHA-256 of exactly the bytes sent'.
findings.recommendation: Give HttpRequest a text-typed body (String) or a validated body accessor, so UTF-8 is guaranteed by construction and no Result or Option arm is needed. Make with_sent_body take impl Into<String>. If a non-UTF-8 body is truly possible, fail with a typed JevError rather than record nothing.
findings.evidence: r-6 sample l.333-343 and D3 l.202-203, 214-216; sc-sha strict-UTF-8 note l.145-153.

findings.issue: Model aliases are stringly typed: ModelAliases::latest(&str) -> Option<ModelId>, with_override(&str, ..), default_model_alias() -> &'static str, and ModelDescriptor::released is a &'static str date. Because lookup is fallible for a built-in backend, the plan adds a provided model_id() whose unwrap_or_else(ModelId::fallback_for(self.id())) builds an Other(UnknownModel) holding a backend id string. That is not a model string, yet it would be logged as model_id. The only guard is test_backend_catalog_roundtrip. A non-catalog backend that does not override model_id() silently logs the catalog's model, which can be wrong after a [models] override.
findings.recommendation: Use a non_exhaustive ModelAlias enum {Jev, Haiku, Luna} with FromStr (CONFIG_INVALID listing valid aliases). Then default_model_alias() and builtin().latest(alias) are infallible, and fallback_for and the unwrap_or_else path can be removed. Consider requiring model_id() on non-built-in backends. A typed release date or an ordering by table position avoids string-date comparison for 'newest'.

findings.issue: Wire answers carry invariants as raw primitives. JevAnswer::Noul { probabilities: BTreeMap<String, f64> } must be 'exactly {yes: p}'. confidence and probabilities are bare f64 in [0,1], checked only in into_answers. CheckResponse::model is String while CheckRequest::model is ModelId. A stray 'confidence' on a noul answer is accepted because deny_unknown_fields is absent.
findings.recommendation: Use a NoulProbabilities { yes } struct with deny_unknown_fields. Use a validated Probability newtype for new jev::v1 and llm::v1 fields where this does not change moved types. Type the response model as ModelId.
findings.evidence: r-5 sample l.231-246 and the response rules l.102-108.

findings.issue: ProjectLabel(Arc<str>) is specified with only new() and as_str(). It has no Display, FromStr, AsRef<str>, Serialize/Deserialize or Hash. The raw-String path is therefore the easy one.

findings.issue: Several new error paths define a code but no recovery hint. Only DecisionSchemaId names its remedy ('hint lists KNOWN'). findings.issue: DecisionSchema is a new public trait in a published crate with no explicit open-or-sealed decision. D5 says new variants are added inside this crate (a SchemaFamily variant, a module and a schema_for arm), so the implementor set is crate-controlled. External implementations would be unusable anyway, since schema_for cannot reach them.
findings.recommendation: Seal it with the private supertrait pattern, or make it pub(crate) until a second variant exists, and document the decision. JudgeBackend stays intentionally open (ADR-SAG-0009); say so in its doc.

findings.issue: DecisionSchema::input returns Result<Self::Input, JevError>, but the only implementation (Canonical) returns the payload unchanged and cannot fail. D4.1 says input_bytes does not call it, so it is a fake-fallible method with no production caller.
findings.recommendation: Return Self::Input directly, or drop the method until a variant needs it.

findings.issue: RunConfig::log_context is optional ('unset: repo = RunConfig's repo_root, project = None'). The default silently yields the worktree root where the log field means the main repository (ADR-SAG-0031), so a caller that skips the setter writes a wrong repo into every row. Correct use depends on compose always remembering to set it.
findings.recommendation: Make the context required at the point the engine emits rows (a constructor argument or a type-level 'configured' state), or have the default call discover_main_repo_root so unset still gives the documented meaning.
findings.evidence: Sample l.345-357 and D5 l.250-253.

findings.issue: Sha256Digest::of(&str) will normalize CRLF and bare CR to LF under sc-sha, but the name and the 'request_sha256 = digest of exactly the bytes sent' contract read as a raw digest. A caller hashing CR-bearing text gets a digest that is not SHA-256 of its bytes. The safety rests on 'compact JSON has no raw CR', which the type does not express.
findings.recommendation: Rename to of_text or document the normalization on the method itself (not only in the sprint doc), so a later caller with CR-bearing input is not surprised.
findings.evidence: D0 l.145-153 and sample l.318.

findings.issue: r-5 replaces parse_outcome with CheckResponse::into_answers. Its stated rule list (lines 103-108, 144-145, and the test_response_rules_rejected cases at line 263) drops two checks the current code enforces. One is response `model` equals the request model. The other is that a choice/score answer's probability keys equal the question's criteria keys. The planned rules only say the choice is a criteria option and the probabilities sum to 1. A reply can therefore carry arbitrary probability labels, or labels that are a subset or superset of the options, and still pass. Those labels then flow into DecisionAnswers, the session document and the r-6 answers_json log column. The noul rule (line 236, `exactly {"yes": p}`) is stated in prose but has no rejection case in the acceptance list (wrong key set, extra `no` key, p outside [0,1]).
findings.recommendation: State in r-5 that into_answers keeps the existing checks: response model equals the request model, and probability keys for choice/score equal the criteria keys. Add the noul key-set and range cases to the existing test_response_rules_rejected list. This carries current behaviour over and adds no new gate. All failures stay RESPONSE_INVALID.
findings.evidence: crates/sc-jev/src/check.rs:94 checks body.model == model, and the parse_outcome doc at lines 80-82 lists answer ids, choice and probability keys matching the request. The r-5 plan rule list at line 103-108 has neither the model check nor the probability-key check.

findings.issue: The request-size limit is enforced today on the final wire body, after the splice. `prepare` compares body.len() to the descriptor's request_limit_bytes and returns InputTooLarge (check.rs:62-66). r-5 deletes splice_model and `prepare`'s path, and deliverables 1 and 3 say no other schema check remains. They never say where the limit is checked against the new CheckRequest::to_body output. The documented Jev body is larger than the canonical bytes (criteria maps, descriptions, model, instructions). A check on the canonical payload would pass bodies that exceed the Jev limit. Dropping the check would send an unbounded body and rely on the server to reject it.
findings.recommendation: State in deliverable 3 that sc-jev compares the length of to_body() output to the Jev descriptor's request_limit_bytes before send. It should return InputTooLarge with the same limit and actual-byte fields as today. This is the existing check moved onto the new builder, not a new gate. Haiku and Luna keep enforce_count_and_message_limits unchanged.
findings.evidence: crates/sc-jev/src/check.rs:62-66 (`let body = splice_model(..); if actual_bytes > limit_bytes { return Err(JevError::input_too_large(..)) }`). r-5 item 1 and item 3 name no replacement site for this check.

findings.issue: Duplicate-key behaviour is unspecified. OrderedMap is a custom order-preserving visitor, and the input_sha256 recovery (item 5) parses the sent body with it. A duplicate question id or criteria key in a recovered body could silently collapse or shadow an entry, giving a digest that differs from prompt_sha256 with no error. Response `answers` is a BTreeMap, where serde keeps the last duplicate id silently.
findings.recommendation: Specify that the OrderedMap visitor and the answers map reject a duplicate key (INPUT_INVALID on request recovery, RESPONSE_INVALID on a reply). Cover it with a case in the existing test_response_rules_rejected and recovery tests rather than a new check.
findings.evidence: r-5 lines 199-203 define OrderedMap with a 'custom visitor' and no duplicate rule. Line 239 and following define `answers: BTreeMap<QuestionId, JevAnswer>`.

findings.topic: HTTP send path and SendTrace hashing
findings.issue: Sha256Digest::of(&str) is declared infallible, but sc-sha's calculate_hash returns a Result (D0, line 145-146 says ShaError::InvalidUtf8 'cannot occur'). The plan does not say what `of` does on an Err. Panicking on the send path (record before every Transport::send) would violate M-PANIC-ON-BUG for a non-bug. Separately, sc-sha normalizes CR and CRLF to LF, so for any text that is not compact serde_json the digest is not SHA-256 of the bytes. The plan covers the committed queries as LF-only. The query text hashed at extract.rs:231 is `input.query`, which can be user-supplied and contain CRLF. Its query_sha256 would then no longer match the bytes it claims to identify.
findings.recommendation: Say that `of` handles the unreachable Err arm without panicking. For example, treat it as a documented unreachable with a deterministic fallback, or keep `of` returning Result at the one send-site call. Note that query_sha256 identifies LF-normalized query text, and keep the 'digest equals SHA-256 of the sent bytes' claim to request bodies only. This is a wording and behaviour clarification, not a new gate.
findings.evidence: r-6 D0 lines 145-159 and the `of` signature at line 318. The `if let Ok(text) = std::str::from_utf8(request.body())` sample at lines 333-337 degrades to a null digest silently, which is acceptable, but `of` itself has no stated error path. crates/sc-treesitter/src/extract.rs:231 hashes input.query.

notes: Worktree HEAD (.git/worktrees/plan-qa2-review/HEAD) is exactly 5836f1befb9550ff4f5125f928cbce0c74e5ef1c. The worktree is detached, as the caller stated, so the branch name could not be verified from it and is echoed from the input.

Service applicability: this is a synchronous ureq-based HTTPS client and CLI. There is no tokio, axum or server listener. Graceful shutdown, health endpoints and backpressure were not reviewed, and nothing was invented for them.

Existing runtime hardening confirmed and unchanged by the plans. ureq_transport.rs sets a 10s connect timeout and a 120s whole-request timeout, HTTPS-only, no redirects. Response bodies are capped at 8 MiB through take(MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES+1). Busy retry is bounded and does not retry errors. The session file read is capped at 8 MiB.

Deliberately not flagged, per the owner rule: the best-effort log-write policy (r-6 D6, test_rejected_log_row_keeps_run_ok), the unscrubbed `project` text, and the repo path column. Log row size is bounded in practice. Answers are tied to the request's criteria keys, which RSH-001 asks to keep, and project is capped at 256 bytes. The rows are written per send with no new lock or shared state.

r-6 record-before-first-send, one SendTrace per backend send, the null request_sha256 when no body is built, and the retry-resends-same-bytes rule are sound as planned. The cancel-before-send case is covered by an acceptance test.
No new gates, receipts or docs-consistency checks are recommended. RSH-001 to RSH-004 are all spec clarifications that carry existing behaviour onto the new code paths.
